source.title: SAM as an Optimal Relaxation of Bayes

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out accuracy for SGD and Adam variants on image-classification datasets; it does not measure the train–test gap or test the paper's broader claim about generalization.
record.gate_note: Table 1, Table 2, and Table 6 report accuracy comparisons for SGD and Adam. Extracted these results for V4. Other table metrics are calibration or uncertainty measures and do not measure the version's held-out performance claim. bSAM's comparisons are its own proposed method and are not cataloged as claim results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own paired held-out accuracy comparisons of Adam and momentum SGD on image classification, bearing on V4. Hyperparameter selection extends beyond learning rates and schedules: Tables 7–8 also vary momentum and L2 regularization. It therefore tests optimizer performance under these recipes, without isolating V4's narrowly limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors establish a conditional theoretical connection between SAM and a relaxed Bayesian objective, derive bSAM to learn variances, and report improved uncertainty estimates and generally competitive or improved held-out accuracy. bSAM does not beat SAM-SGD in every setting.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SGD and Adam baselines as part of experiments on a proposed Bayesian-SAM method; does not reproduce the cited optimizer studies. Image-classification training uses moderate grid search for validation accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset and augmentation condition; Adam trails SGD in reported paired test-accuracy comparisons, with smaller differences on MNIST and FashionMNIST than on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed total batch size 128, splitting SAM-SGD minibatches into 1 versus 16 perturbation subbatches increases CIFAR-100 accuracy from 55.88% to 59.51%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The subbatch size used to compute SAM perturbations affects held-out performance. This does not establish V5's penalty from increasing the actual optimizer batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical SAM–Bayes connection and bSAM accuracy and uncertainty improvements do not measure a correlation between magnitude-aware sharpness and train–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM admits a relaxed Bayesian interpretation that motivates an uncertainty-estimating optimizer.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison reports validation/test accuracy but no training performance, so it cannot establish a train–test generalization gap. The text says hyperparameters were selected by a moderate grid search, but does not provide enough detail here to establish the relative tuning budget for each optimizer.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were left out. ResNet-18 Adam comparisons are not reported in Table 2, so no result rows were created for those conditions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; comparative tuning-budget effects; training performance; language benchmarks; switching optimizers; and decoupled weight decay.
Changing the actual training batch size under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipes.
Dropout effects and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking measured train–test gaps against norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Paired SAM-Adam versus SAM-SGD accuracy comparisons are omitted although they bear on optimizer ordering under a shared SAM objective. Without augmentation: CIFAR-10 85.26 versus 87.49, CIFAR-100 53.25 versus 58.58. With augmentation: CIFAR-10 91.57 versus 92.29, CIFAR-100 65.34 versus 67.27, TinyImageNet 51.17 versus 52.25. Small datasets: MNIST 98.58 versus 98.82, FashionMNIST 91.66 versus 91.95. Add linked rows before assigning verdicts to these conditions; the direction agrees with V4, with smaller differences in several settings.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. There are seven plain Adam–SGD paired conditions, not five. Section 4 describes metrics as evaluated on the validation set, while Appendix G also uses validation accuracy for hyperparameter selection; an independent test-set protocol is not clearly established in the supplied text. Broader hyperparameter tuning here does not itself test whether broadening tuning removes an optimizer gap.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Training performance comparisons; language benchmarks; broader tuning, switching optimizers, and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size sweep and fixed-epoch large-batch penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with the train–test gap.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ResNet-20-FRN on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 without augmentation, and CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet with augmentation; moderate grid search including momentum and L2 regularization.
relationships.reason: R1–R10 show Adam below momentum SGD by 1.71–16.09 accuracy points; this supports the held-out optimizer ordering under these recipes.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam accuracy than momentum SGD across the augmentation settings remains unverified.

relationships.condition: MLP on MNIST and LeNet-5 on FashionMNIST.
relationships.reason: R15–R18 show only small Adam deficits, 0.22 and 0.23 accuracy points; the FashionMNIST difference is comparable to seed variation.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly trailed SGD slightly, with the FashionMNIST difference comparable to seed variation, but these comparisons remain unverified.
